source_text:
Διὸ ὑπακούσωμεν τῇ μεγαλοπρεπεῖ καὶ ἐνδόξῳ βουλήσει αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἱκέται γενόμενοι τοῦ ἐλέους καὶ τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ προσπέσωμεν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωμεν ἐπὶ τοὺς οἰκτιρμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ἀπολιπόντες τὴν ματαιοπονίαν τήν τε ἔριν καὶ τὸ εἰς θάνατον ἄγον ζῆλος.
ἀτενίσωμεν εἰς τοὺς τελείως λειτουργήσαντας τῇ μεγαλοπρεπεῖ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ.
λάβωμεν Ἐνώχ, ὃς ἐν ὑπακοῇ δίκαιος εὑρεθεὶς μετετέθη, καὶ οὐχ εὑρέθη αὐτοῦ θάνατος.
Νῶε πιστὸς εὑρεθεὶς διὰ τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ παλιγγενεσίαν κόσμῳ ἐκήρυξεν, καὶ διέσωσεν δἰ αὐτοῦ ὁ δεσπότης τὰ εἰσελθόντα ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ ζῶα εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν.
thought_title: Obey God's will and turn from envy to the examples of Enoch and Noah
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, has just quoted Isaiah's call to repentance and now urges the Corinthians to obey God's will and look to ancient examples of faithful ministry.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore let us obey the magnificent and glorious will of him, and having become suppliants of the mercy and of the kindness of him let us fall down and let us turn to the compassions of him, having left behind the vain toil, both the strife and the leading to death envy. Let us look intently at the ones who perfectly ministered to the magnificent glory of him. Let us take Enoch, who in obedience having been found righteous was translated, and was not found of him death. Noah having been found faithful through the ministry of him a regeneration to the world proclaimed, and saved through him the master the having entered in harmony living creatures into the ark.

choices.why: The compound noun means labor that is empty or futile; 'vain toil' preserves the sense of wasted effort without importing a modern idiom.

choices.english: the envy that leads to death
choices.why: The participle phrase 'leading to death' modifies envy; rendering it as a relative clause keeps the causal force clear in English.
The verb means to be transferred or removed from one place to another; 'translated' is the traditional English term for Enoch's removal without death.

choices.english: proclaimed a regeneration to the world
choices.why: The dative κόσμῳ marks the recipient of the proclamation; 'to the world' keeps that dative force explicit.
rejected: announced a new birth to the world
heralded a rebirth for the world

choices.english: the living creatures that entered in harmony
choices.why: The participle 'having entered' plus the dative of manner 'in harmony' describes how the animals entered the ark; the rendering keeps the manner phrase attached to the entering.
rejected: the animals that entered in concord
the living things that went in with one accord
the creatures that entered in unity

bible_refs.note: Enoch was translated and was not found because God translated him
Noah was found righteous and faithful
Noah and the living creatures entered the ark

pass_b_english: Therefore let us obey his magnificent and glorious will. Let us fall before him as suppliants of his mercy and goodness, and turn to his compassions. Let us leave behind the vain toil, the strife, and the envy that leads to death.
Let us look intently at those who ministered perfectly to his magnificent glory.
Let us take Enoch. He was found righteous in obedience, and he was translated, and no death of his was found.
Noah was found faithful. Through his ministry he proclaimed a regeneration to the world, and through him the Master saved the living creatures that entered the ark in harmony.

problems.why: λάβωμεν is first person plural hortatory subjunctive ('let us take'), not imperative 'Take'. The English 'Take Enoch' reads as imperative to the reader, changing the exhortatory 'let us' to a command, and loses the inclusivity of the author's appeal.
problems.fix: Let us take Enoch as an example
problems.ruling: λάβωμεν is hortatory subjunctive 'let us take'; 'Take Enoch' reads as imperative, losing the inclusive exhortation.

problems.why: First person plural hortatory 'let us take' changed to second person imperative 'Take'. The author includes himself in the exhortation; English excludes author and commands reader.
problems.ruling: Duplicate of #1; λάβωμεν is hortatory 'let us take,' not second-person imperative 'Take.'

edits.old: Take Enoch: he was found righteous
edits.new: Let us take Enoch: he was found righteous

fixed: The gloss already renders λάβωμεν as 'Let us take', so no gloss edit is needed.
The English 'Take Enoch' was changed to 'Let us take Enoch' to restore the first-person plural hortatory sense.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer units, clarified the implied subject of the first paragraph, and separated the examples of Enoch and Noah into distinct paragraphs for easier reading aloud.
